title: Add SpaceFile type: flat blob-based shared files in core chat draft
description:
Decision (Mark, 2026-11-02): Spaces get BOTH FileNode (optional, draft-atwood-jmap-chat-filenode-00, unchanged) AND a simple blob-based shared-files layer in the core draft (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00). Source: ~/Cache/crate-jmap-handoff-2026-10-22/spacefile-brief-for-spec-session.md. Do not edit drafts until this bead is worked.

Chosen shape ("option 2"): new flat top-level type, working name SpaceFile.
- Properties: id, spaceId, blobId, name, type (media type), size, created, uploader (sender identity as the draft already models it; cf. senderId).
- Flat on purpose: no folders, no per-file ACL, no inheritance. Space roles decide everything: "send" may upload; "manage_channels" may delete/rename; "view" may read. Non-members get nothing.
- Independent of Messages (unlike Attachment, which dies with its message), like Slack/Discord shared files.
- Methods: SpaceFile/get, /changes, /set, /query, /queryChanges; filter at least by spaceId. Space closedAt rules apply as for other Space objects.
- Size limits: reuse or parallel maxAttachmentBytes; per-Space quota open.
- Interop: a server that also implements chat-filenode MAY mirror SpaceFiles into the Space tree; state allowed, not required.
- Crate note: new type is additive for the crates (can land after crate 0.5.0). Do NOT add a field to the Space object.

Rejected alternative: derived view = query over message attachments, no new type. Rejected because files cannot outlive their messages.

Open questions:
1. Name: SpaceFile vs SharedFile.
2. uploader field shape.
3. Per-Space quota.
4. Whether rename is allowed.
5. Interaction with SpaceBan / member removal (do the uploader's files stay?).
6. Federation of SpaceFile across servers.

Keyword discipline: per bcp14-keyword-discipline memory, MUST only where interop breaks; role/access checks are SHOULD.
notes:
Motivation (Mark, 2026-11-02 crate session): FileNode is WebDAV-shaped (inherited ACLs, onExists modes, depth semantics, roles) and its churn (-19 rights model, onExists, depth; -20 one-role-per-account, see jmap-chat-spec-8g3r) has cost repeated tracking work. SpaceFile gives Spaces a file area that does not depend on FileNode. Keep it flat (no hierarchy, no per-file rights) so it cannot grow into a second FileNode. Also rejected: dropping the chat-filenode binding entirely; Mark chose BOTH.
Open question 7: labels. Should SpaceFile carry labels (Gmail/JMAP-Mailbox style, many-to-many, flat) for organisation instead of folders? Gives grouping without move/cycle/collision/ACL-inheritance rules. Labels carry no permissions; Space roles still decide access. Undecided; may be a later additive extension rather than core.
Rationale for Q7 'labels carry no permissions' (keep firm): Google Drive allowed multi-parent files until 2020, then forced single-parent + shortcuts because inherited rights from multiple parents made effective access unknowable. Single-parent folders exist largely to make inherited ACLs tractable. Gmail labels avoid this because labels never grant access. If SpaceFile gets labels, they SHOULD stay out of access control (Space roles only) - else we rebuild Drive's problem.
Related: jmap-chat-spec-glm3 (generic bags extension; SpaceFile stays flat).
Decision (Mark, 2026-11-02): FileNode + SpaceFile coexistence is left to implementations; spec does not dictate. Specifically, each is a server/client choice: (a) whether attaching a file to a Message also creates a SpaceFile; (b) whether a server that implements chat-filenode mirrors SpaceFiles into the Space tree (keep as MAY, neither required nor forbidden); (c) how clients present both. Spec text should only: describe the purpose of each (SpaceFile = flat Space shared files, Space roles; FileNode = optional document tree, its own rights); state the permissive MAYs; note that both reference immutable blobs so copying between them is a plain create with the same blobId; say no rights inheritance between the two models. Clients learn about server-created SpaceFiles via SpaceFile/changes like any other object, so no extra mechanism needed.
